title: Ex 7.2 (⇒) · If x is odd, then 3x + 6 is odd
prompt: Let $x$ be an integer. Exercise 7.2 says $x$ is odd if and only if $3x + 6$ is odd. This problem is one direction of that if-and-only-if: prove that if $x$ is odd, then $3x + 6$ is odd. Use direct proof. (The converse (⇐) direction is a separate problem.)
answer_format: A structured proof: let, case, expr and witness steps (notes optional). No final answer box.
hints: Write x = 2a + 1 with a let step.
solution: Suppose $x$ is odd, so $x = 2a + 1$ for some integer $a$.
Then $3x + 6 = 6a + 9 = 2(3a + 4) + 1$, and $3a + 4$ is an integer, so $3x + 6$ is odd. $\blacksquare$

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses if-and-only-if proof (Section 7.1): this is the forward (⇒) direction, by direct proof, with Definitions 4.1, 4.2 (even, odd).
